name: hvac-canonical-ots
instr:
The repository at `/workdir` is hvac, a Python client for the HashiCorp Vault HTTP API: the `Client` class,
its HTTP adapters and error handling, the auth method classes (AppRole, AWS, Azure, certificates, GCP, GitHub,
JWT/OIDC, Kubernetes, LDAP, legacy MFA, Okta, RADIUS, tokens, userpass) and the secrets engine classes (KV versions 1
and 2, Transit, Transform, PKI, SSH, databases, identity, AWS, Azure, GCP, LDAP, Active Directory, Consul,
RabbitMQ), each of which turns method calls into Vault API requests.

Fix all implementation drift from the documentation in this repository.
Everything in scope is the hvac client core (hvac/__init__.py, hvac/v1/, hvac/adapters.py, hvac/utils.py, hvac/exceptions.py, hvac/aws_utils.py, hvac/constants/ and the API base modules hvac/api/__init__.py, hvac/api/vault_api_base.py and hvac/api/vault_api_category.py), the auth methods package hvac/api/auth_methods/ and the secrets engines package hvac/api/secrets_engines/, together with the documentation pages README.md, docs/overview.rst, docs/advanced_usage.rst and every page under docs/usage/auth_methods/ and docs/usage/secrets_engines/, and the module, class and function docstrings of the in-scope modules.

Where the code and the documentation disagree about runtime behavior, the documentation is the
authority: change the implementation so that it does what the documentation says, and do not edit
or delete documentation to make a disagreement go away. The documentation is those pages and the
